title: Eviction safety
objection: Redis will silently delete my data when it fills up.

claims.claim: allkeys-lru destroyed 19,965 of 20,000 durable records (99.8%), with 0 errors raised
claims.detail: Redis evicted 294,700 keys and reported success on every single write. The data is gone and nothing told the application. This is the objection, and it is completely valid.
every allkeys-* policy treats your primary records as cache. The word "allkeys" is not decoration.

claims.claim: volatile-ttl preserved all 20,000/20,000 durable records while evicting 293,855 cache keys
claims.detail: keys written without a TTL are not eviction candidates under any volatile-* policy — so "is this row durable?" becomes "did I set a TTL?", which is a decision you make per write

claims.claim: noeviction preserved all 20,000 records and raised 2,181 OOM errors instead of deleting anything
claims.detail: the write fails, synchronously, on the connection that caused it — an incident you can page on, rather than a silent corruption you discover next quarter

claims.claim: the error is explicit and machine-readable: "OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'.…"
claims.detail: clients can detect the OOM prefix and shed load, rather than silently succeeding against a shrinking dataset

oomMessage: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'.
